end.summary:
Identified Bishnoi, sacred groves, and the Chipko movement as nature-protecting traditions.
Explained that roots hold soil and sacred groves protect plants and animals.
Connected neem leaves keeping insects away with observations and science.
Early mix-up between Bishnoi and Chipko was separated later using a timeline.
Final recap included Khejarli, Chipko in 1973, and present-day sacred groves.
end.parentNote: Asha practised examples of traditional nature protection and linked them to science, such as roots holding soil and neem leaves discouraging insects. Dev used a useful timeline in the final recap; an early mix-up between Bishnoi tree protection and Chipko was corrected later in the lesson. At home, ask Dev to make three picture boxes labelled Bishnoi, Chipko, and sacred groves, with one fact in each.
